full_text_zh:
[P1] 树上开花

[P2] 南北朝时期，中国的南方和北方分成了两个国家。南边的宋朝，皇帝姓刘，所以称刘宋；北边的魏国就叫北魏。
刘宋和北魏不是一对好邻居，他们常常你一拳我一脚，打得难分难解。有一年，刘宋皇帝就派了征南大将军檀道济，去攻打北魏，要夺回被北魏占去的土地。

[P3] 行军路上，北魏大将率领一支轻骑兵，一会儿在前面拦截檀道济，一会儿在后面追击他；一会儿从左边杀过来，一会儿又从右边冲过去，搅得檀道济手下的士兵心里发慌，马也到处乱跑。檀道济停下来，想跟北魏军好好打一仗，可是那些轻骑兵又一溜烟跑掉了。

[P4] 一天晚上，檀道济正在帐营中看兵书。突然，一名士兵惊慌地闯了进来，大叫道："大将军，不好了，我们的粮草被北魏军烧了！"檀道济吃了一惊，急忙扔下手中的兵书说："快去救粮草！"等他带着士兵来到粮草营地时，发现大部分粮草已经烧着了，檀道济忍不住连连摇头叹气。

[P5] 粮草被烧，又没有新的
运送过来，檀道济只好
带着大军调头往回走。
可是粮草只剩下一点点，
士兵们每顿都吃不饱，
哪有力气赶路呀。没过
几天，就有人忍受不了
饥饿，悄悄地掉队，叛
逃到了北魏军那边。

[P6] 在北魏军营中吃了顿饱饭，
叛逃的刘宋士兵满脸堆笑，
对北魏大将点头哈腰地说：
"将军，我告诉您一个秘密。
自从北魏军烧了刘宋军的粮
草，他们就没粮吃了。您现
在带兵追上去，肯定能把檀
道济一举消灭！"北魏大将一
听，脸上笑开了花。

[P7] 檀道济曾在战场上斩杀了好几位北魏将军，北魏人都恨他恨得牙痒痒，这下可以找他报仇了。北魏大将立刻带着全军，追赶檀道济去了。檀道济现在心里十分着急。北魏军在屁股后面甩不掉，眼看就要追上来了。士兵们吃不饱肚子，天天有气无力的。这样下去，北魏军不用打，刘宋军就败了呀！

[P8] 檀道济双眉紧锁，苦想办法。眼下，刘宋军最大的危机就是缺粮！北魏军敢追过来，也是因为他们知道，刘宋军断粮了。怎样才能让北魏军相信，刘宋军的粮草还多得很，不敢再追上来呢？

[P9] 檀道济在营帐中踱来踱去，
没想出好办法。于是，他走出营帐，来到了附近的河边。
河滩上的大石头间，有几块小小的沙滩，黄昏的阳光一照，黄沙像金子一样闪闪发光。士兵们东一堆，西一堆，正躺在大石头上，懒洋洋地晒着太阳。看着这些亮闪闪的沙子，檀道济灵机一动，有了主意。

[P10] 太阳落山了，天色渐渐暗下来。北魏军追上来，围住了刘宋军的军营。不出意外，他们明天就要发动进攻了！
这时，从檀道济的营帐中，悄悄地钻出几道黑影。他们推着小车，来到河滩上，挖起河滩上的沙子，拉到了粮草营地。一趟又一趟，不一会儿，粮草营地的沙子就堆得像小山一样高了。

[P11] 这时，粮草营地的火把点亮了。檀道济大声命令道："今天晚上，你们盘算一下剩下的粮食。过两天，后方的粮草就要运来了，得腾出地方呀！"士兵们急忙支起粮囤，取出米斗，舀起了沙子。他们装满一斗，就哗啦啦倒进粮囤里，嘴里还大声唱着数："一斗！两斗！……一石！两石！……"

[P12] 不一会儿，一个粮囤就装满了。檀道济叫人在顶上铺一层白米，远远看去，真像是一座米山。这样量了一囤又一囤，一直量了一晚上。第二天清早，小麻雀在粮囤上飞来飞去啄米吃。刘宋士兵们看到一囤囤的白米，以为新的粮草送来了，都高兴得欢呼起来，一下子有了力气。

[P13] 北魏军的探子一早就远远看到了
刘宋军的米山，又想起昨天晚上
听到的量米声，赶紧去报告主
帅：“谁说刘宋军断粮了？我看他
们的粮食堆了一囤又一囤。现在
可不能跟檀道济决战，我们会输
得很惨的！”北魏大将一听，以为
自己上当了，拍着桌子大喊道。

[P14] "那两个投降的士兵就是诱饵，想引着我们往陷阱里跳呢！气死我了，快快快，把他们绑出去斩了！"
见北魏军不敢进攻，檀道济知道自己的量沙计奏效了。他叫将士们把剩余的军粮全煮了，大家饱饱地吃了一顿。然后，他命将士们穿上铠甲，自己则穿着一件白袍，骑着白马，打开了营门。

[P15] 檀道济骑马走在前面，将士们排着整齐的队伍跟在后面，大家不慌不忙，慢慢地向外走去。北魏军看见，都怔住了。
"檀道济诡计多端，这会儿又在耍什么花招？不好，周围肯定有伏兵！"北魏大将这样想着，不但没敢进攻，反而吓得往后撤退了老远，眼睁睁地看着檀道济带着军队跑了。

[P16] 刘宋军的粮草被烧光，如果北魏军知道实情，只要围困他们，就能轻松取胜。而檀道济想逃脱，就像“铁树开花”一样难。如何让“铁树开花”，逃出北魏军的包围呢？檀道济用沙子装满粮囤，再铺上一层白米，就像给铁树贴上了美丽的假花。北魏军被吓住，不敢进攻，檀道济就带着将士顺利逃生了。像这样以假乱真，唬住敌人的计策，就叫“树上开花”。
full_text_en:
[P1] Flowers Bloom on the Tree

[P2] During the Northern and Southern Dynasties period, China was divided into two countries: the Southern Song Dynasty and the Northern Wei Dynasty. The Southern Song Dynasty, whose emperor bore the surname Liu, was called Liu Song; the Northern Wei Dynasty was simply called Northern Wei.
Liu Song and Northern Wei were not good neighbors. They often fought fiercely, hitting each other with fists and feet, unable to resolve their conflicts. One year, the emperor of Liu Song sent General Tan Daoji, the Commander of the Southern Campaign, to attack Northern Wei and reclaim the land that had been occupied by Northern Wei.

[P3] On the march, a Northern Wei general led a force of light cavalry, sometimes blocking Tan Daoji from the front, sometimes chasing him from behind; sometimes attacking from the left, sometimes charging from the right, causing Tan Daoji's soldiers to panic and their horses to run wildly. Tan Daoji stopped, wanting to fight a proper battle with the Northern Wei army, but those light cavalrymen vanished like smoke again.

[P4] One night, Tan Daoji was reading military books in his tent. Suddenly, a soldier rushed in in panic, shouting: "General, trouble! Our supplies have been burned by the Northern Wei army!" Tan Daoji was startled and quickly dropped his book, saying: "Hurry, save the supplies!" When he arrived at the supply camp with his soldiers, he found most of the supplies already burning. Tan Daoji couldn't help but shake his head and sigh repeatedly.

[P5] The grain supplies were burned, and no new supplies had arrived. So, Tan Daoji had to turn his army around and head back.
But there was only a little grain left. The soldiers couldn't eat enough at each meal—how could they have the strength to march? After a few days, some couldn't bear the hunger anymore, quietly dropped out of the ranks, and defected to the Northern Wei army.

[P6] After eating a full meal in the Northern Wei camp,
the defected Liu Song soldier, beaming with smiles,
bowed to the Northern Wei general and said:
"General, I have a secret to tell you.
Ever since the Northern Wei army burned the Liu Song army's supplies,
they've had no food left. If you lead your troops to chase them now,
you're sure to eliminate Tan Daoji completely!" The Northern Wei general,
upon hearing this, broke into a wide grin.

[P7] Tandaoji had killed several Northern Wei generals on the battlefield before. The Northern Wei people hated him to the point of gnashing their teeth—now they could finally get revenge. The Northern Wei general immediately led his entire army to chase after Tandaoji. Tandaoji was now extremely anxious. The Northern Wei army was right behind them, impossible to shake off, and was about to catch up. The soldiers were starving, weak and listless every day. If this continued, the Northern Wei army wouldn’t even need to fight—the Song army would collapse on its own!

[P8] Tandaoji frowned deeply, struggling to think of a solution. At present, the biggest crisis for the Liu Song army was a lack of food! The Northern Wei army dared to pursue them because they knew the Liu Song army had run out of supplies. How could he make the Northern Wei army believe that the Liu Song army still had plenty of grain and dared not pursue any further?

[P9] Tandaoji paced back and forth in his tent, 
unable to come up with a good plan. So, he stepped out of the tent and went to the nearby riverbank.
Between the large rocks on the riverbank, there were a few small sandy patches. Under the evening sun, the yellow sand sparkled like gold. Soldiers lay in groups, here and there, lazily basking in the sun on the big rocks. Seeing these sparkling grains of sand, Tandaoji suddenly had an idea.

[P10] The sun had set, and the sky was gradually growing dark. The Northern Wei army caught up and surrounded the Liu Song army's camp. As expected, they would launch an attack tomorrow!
At this moment, several dark figures quietly emerged from Tan Daoji's tent. They pushed small carts to the riverbank, dug up sand from the shore, and transported it to the grain and fodder camp. Trip after trip, in no time, the sand in the camp had piled up like a small mountain.

[P11] At this moment, the torches in the grain camp were lit. Tan Daoji shouted orders: "Tonight, count the remaining grain. In two days, the supply convoy will arrive, so we must clear space!" The soldiers hurriedly set up grain bins, took out measuring scoops, and scooped up sand. They filled each scoop and poured it哗啦啦 into the bins, loudly counting aloud: "One dou! Two dou! ... One shi! Two shi! ..."

[P12] In no time, a grain silo was filled. Tan Daoji had people spread a layer of white rice on top; from afar, it looked just like a mountain of rice. They filled one silo after another, continuing all through the night. The next morning, sparrows flew around the silos, pecking at the rice. The Liu Song soldiers saw pile after pile of white rice, thinking fresh supplies had arrived. They cheered with joy and suddenly felt full of strength.

[P13] The Northern Wei scouts, as early as morning, saw from afar the mountain of rice belonging to the Liu Song army. Remembering the sound of measuring rice they had heard the night before, they hurried to report to their commander: "Who said the Liu Song army was out of food? I can see their grain piled up in one granary after another. We must not fight a decisive battle against Tan Daoji now, or we will lose badly!" The Northern Wei general, upon hearing this, thought he had been tricked, and slammed his fist on the table, shouting.

[P14] "Those two surrendering soldiers were bait, trying to lure us into a trap! I'm furious, quickly, quickly, tie them up and execute them!"
Seeing the Northern Wei army dared not attack, Tan Daoji knew his sand-measuring ruse had worked. He ordered his soldiers to cook all the remaining grain, and everyone ate a full meal. Then, he commanded his soldiers to put on their armor, while he himself wore a white robe and rode a white horse, opening the camp gate.

[P15] Tandaoji rode at the front, with his soldiers marching in neat formation behind him. Everyone remained calm and composed, slowly moving outward. The Northern Wei troops saw this and were stunned.
"Tandaoji is full of tricks—what scheme is he up to now? No good, there must be ambushes around!" The Northern Wei general thought, and not only did he refrain from attacking, but he also retreated far back in fear, watching helplessly as Tandaoji led his army away.

[P16] The grain supplies of the Liu Song army were burned to ashes. If the Northern Wei army knew the truth, they could easily win by simply surrounding them. For Tan Daoji to escape would be as difficult as "a iron tree blooming." How to make the "iron tree bloom" and escape from the Northern Wei army's encirclement? Tan Daoji filled the grain silos with sand and then covered them with a layer of white rice, just like pasting beautiful fake flowers onto an iron tree. The Northern Wei army was frightened and dared not attack, so Tan Daoji led his soldiers to escape safely. Such a strategy of deceiving the enemy with falsehoods is called "flowers blooming on a tree."
full_summary_zh:
[P1] 本页标题为“树上开花”，画面中一名身穿铠甲的武将正愤怒地拍打桌子，桌上木屑飞溅，旁边放着一个绿色小罐。
[P2] 本页介绍了南北朝时期刘宋与北魏的对立背景，并说明刘宋皇帝派遣征南大将军檀道济率军攻打北魏，意图夺回被占领的土地。画面描绘了檀道济率军出征的场景，以及北魏城池的守将。
[P3] 本页描绘了檀道济率军行进途中，遭遇北魏轻骑兵的反复骚扰，士兵惊慌、战马失控，檀道济欲战却敌军遁逃的场景。
[P4] 本页描绘了檀道济在军营中读书时，突然得知粮草被北魏军烧毁，他急忙带兵前往救援，却发现大部分粮草已烧毁，不禁摇头叹息。
[P5] 粮草被烧毁后，檀道济率军撤退，士兵因饥饿难耐，有人悄悄叛逃至北魏军中。
[P6] 叛逃的刘宋士兵向北魏大将透露檀道济军队因粮草被烧而断粮，北魏大将听后大喜，准备追击。
[P7] 本页描绘了檀道济率军撤退途中，因粮草被毁导致士兵饥饿，士气低落，而北魏大军紧追不舍，形势危急。
[P8] 檀道济在军营中苦思对策，因粮草被毁导致军队断粮，他担忧北魏军追击，思考如何制造假象让敌军误以为己方粮草充足。
[P9] 檀道济在军营中苦思对策未果，便来到河边，看到黄昏下闪闪发光的沙子，灵机一动，想出了应对粮草被毁的计策。
[P10] 檀道济在北魏军围困军营、准备进攻的危急时刻，命人将河滩上的沙子运到粮草营地，堆成小山，为后续的‘沙中藏粮’计策做准备。
[P11] 檀道济命令士兵在粮草营地用沙子装满粮囤，并大声报数，制造粮草充足的假象，以迷惑敌军。
[P12] 檀道济命士兵用沙子装满粮囤，并在顶部铺上白米，制造粮草充足的假象。士兵们看到后误以为粮草已到，士气大振。
[P13] 北魏军探子发现刘宋军粮草堆积如山，并听到量米声，误以为对方粮草充足，急忙报告主帅。北魏大将听后以为中计，惊慌失措，拍桌大喊。
[P14] 北魏军探子误以为刘宋军粮草充足而不敢进攻，檀道济趁机让士兵煮食剩余军粮，随后自己身穿白袍骑白马，命士兵披甲打开营门，准备反击。
[P15] 檀道济率军从容出营，北魏军误以为有伏兵，惊慌撤退，刘宋军趁机安全撤离。
[P16] 本页总结了檀道济用沙子装满粮囤并覆盖白米，制造粮草充足的假象，成功吓退北魏军并安全撤离的计策，该计策被称为“树上开花”。
